title: HR and Payroll Officer
company: Not For Profit People - Agency - Permanent
description:
HR and Payroll Officer

Are you an organised and people-focused HR professional with payroll experience who enjoys delivering excellent service and building strong working relationships?

We are seeking an enthusiastic HR and Payroll Officer to join the Human Resources team in this full-time, permanent role.

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full employee lifecycle while building expertise in both HR and payroll. It is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing attention to detail with relationship-building and who takes pride in delivering a high-quality service.

Position: HR & Payroll Officer

Location: Kidlington, Oxford/hybrid

Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Salary: £37,751.95 - £40,655.94 per annum

Contract: Permanent

Closing Date: Midnight on Tuesday 18 November 2026. Interviews will take place at Church House, Oxford: Friday 27 November 2026

The Role

You will join the Human Resources team, playing a key role in supporting employees, clergy, managers and senior leaders across the Diocese. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to meaningful work, ensuring people are supported through efficient payroll, recruitment, learning and development, and employee lifecycle processes.

This is a varied and rewarding role within a professional and collaborative HR team that supports both the Diocesan Board of Finance and Diocesan Board of Education. You will provide reliable, confidential and people-centred HR and payroll support that helps employees, clergy and leaders do their best work.

You will also play a key role in delivering recruitment and onboarding activities, be the first point of contact for payroll-related matters and will help maintain robust controls and ensure compliance with statutory and organisational requirements.

About You

We are looking for an experienced HR and payroll professional who is highly organised, accurate and customer-focused, with a passion for providing excellent support and advice. You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, handling sensitive information with discretion and working collaboratively with a wide range of stakeholders.

You will bring experience of HR administration and payroll processing within a busy organisational environment, together with strong communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

You will also have:
- Sound knowledge of generalist HR practices and payroll administration.
- Up-to-date knowledge of UK employment legislation and HMRC requirements relating to payroll, tax and statutory payments.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, learning and development, employee relations and performance management activities.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, and experience using HR management systems and payroll systems.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail, particularly when working with payroll and employee data and maintaining accurate employee records.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

A CIPD and/or CIPP qualification or membership would be advantageous, although applications are welcomed from candidates with transferable skills and experience.

You do not need to be a practising Christian to work here. Around half of staff are not practising Christians, but all are comfortable working within the Christian ethos and values that underpin the organisation's work.

The successful candidate must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews. We are particularly keen to receive applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority heritage and disabled candidates, who are currently underrepresented.

You may have experience in other areas such as HR, Human Resources, Personnel, People, HR Officer, Human Resources Officer, Personnel Officer, People Officer, Payroll, Payroll Officer, Payroll Assistant, HR Assistant, Finance Officer, Finance Assistant, HR and Finance, HR and Payroll.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People.

title: Executive Assistant
description:
Who we are and what we do

We, Hachette UK Distribution, are the leading book distribution company in the UK. We are one of the most advanced distribution centres in Europe, with leading-edge automation and modern systems which will ensure world-class service to customers and publisher clients. We ship in excess of 80 million books globally each year and supply one out of every four books to the UK trade.

Our mission is to make it easy for everyone to discover new worlds of ideas, learning, entertainment and opportunity.

Hachette UK Distribution is part of the Hachette UK publishing group.

What you'll be doing

We're looking for an accomplished Executive Assistant to provide trusted administrative and organisational support to the HUKD CEO, with ad hoc support for the wider leadership team. You'll help keep day-to-day operations running smoothly, ensuring the CEO can focus on key priorities and assisting the successful delivery of events at our site.

This is a varied, hands-on role for someone who enjoys anticipating needs, solving problems and bringing order to a fast-moving environment. From diary and inbox management to events, travel, communications and project support, you'll act as a professional and discreet partner to senior leaders and stakeholders.

This is an on-site part time role, totalling 20 hours per week, Monday to Friday 9:30am to 1:30pm.
- Manage a busy, fast-moving diary, balancing competing priorities and resolving clashes before they arise.
- Review and prioritise emails, calls and invitations, responding directly or drafting correspondence on behalf of the CEO.
- Maintain efficient inbox and file-management systems for key information and documents.
- Organise regular meetings with internal and external stakeholders.
- Draft and coordinate site communications, bringing together contributions from across the business.
- Prepare, format and proofread high-quality presentations, reports and confidential documents.
- Plan off-site strategy days, client meetings, lunches and evening events, working closely with venues and suppliers.
- Coordinate site events in partnership with third-party suppliers and Facilities teams.
- Support projects through activity coordination, action tracking, data analysis and presentations

Who we are looking for
- Proven experience supporting senior executives as an Executive Assistant or in an equivalent role.
- Excellent organisation, prioritisation and forward-planning skills, with the ability to manage changing demands and deadlines.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the judgement to reflect the CEO's and company's tone.
- Experience coordinating events, venues, catering and third-party suppliers.
- Experience supporting projects, presentations and senior leadership teams.
- Confidence using Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint, with the ability to learn new systems and processes.
- Sound judgement, initiative and confidence working independently.
- A collaborative, credible and approachable style, with strong stakeholder-management skills.
- Exceptional attention to detail and a proactive, can-do approach.
- The ability to remain calm under pressure and handle sensitive information with complete confidentiality and discretion.

What we offer

Our people are our greatest asset and our benefits reflect this. Therefore, we offer an extensive list of benefits that include:
- 35 days annual holiday including Bank Holidays
- Pension Plan and Life Assurance schemes
- Company enhanced family policy including maternity, paternity and shared parental
- Reward programme giving discounts, savings and cash back at numerous retailers
- 2 Community Days per year
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Eye care vouchers
- Generous discounts on books we publish
- Mental Health First Aiders / Champions and an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
- Wide-ranging training library
- Development Programmes including Mentoring
- Staff Events
- Many employee networks to join
- Free onsite parking
- Free tea and coffee

Our commitment

Hachette employs people on the basis of their abilities. We aim to attract and develop talent from a base as broad as the world of readers we want to reach, with a wide and representative range of age, faith, disability, race, gender, sexuality and socio-economic, regional and cultural backgrounds.

If you are shortlisted and need us to make any adjustments to help you attend your interview, please let us know.

We will notify all candidates of the outcome of their application.

title: Technical Publications Administrator
company: PLANET RECRUITMENT SERVICES LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:
Position: Technical Publications Administrator
Hours: 37 hours per week
Location: Abingdon
Salary: £28,000 - £35,000 per annum

The employer works with medical devices and associated products, where clear, accurate documentation supports safe use, consistent production and effective servicing. This role offers the opportunity to turn complex mechanical and electronic information into practical instructions that people can confidently follow.

The Role:
As a Technical Publications Administrator you will work within Technical Publications, collaborating with New Product Development, Quality and Regulatory, Production, Engineering and other subject matter experts. Your objective will be to create, maintain and publish accurate, compliant documentation, from Instructions for Use (IFUs) and service manuals to production procedures, datasheets and product artwork.

Reporting to the Technical Publications Manager, you will take ownership of assigned work and follow established Publications and Quality Management System (QMS) processes. Following appropriate training, you will work independently, managing documents through review, approval and publication. The position has no direct reports.

Main Responsibilities:
Create, revise and continuously improve IFUs, user manuals, service manuals, datasheets, production procedures and work instructions.
Gather and verify technical information and applicable regulatory requirements with colleagues across the business, ensuring procedures accurately reflect approved production practices.
Coordinate document reviews and approvals, manage updates through formal change control and maintain supporting records.
Observe and photograph production processes, turning the information into clear assembly and test procedures supported by photographs, illustrations and other visual aids.
Create and update technical illustrations, product artwork, labels and symbols, and proofread, edit and format documents using desktop-publishing software.
Arrange external translations, reviewing and reformatting translated documentation as required.
Prepare files for external printing, check printer proofs and support in-house printing of user manuals and other documentation needed by Production.
Apply company templates, style guides and branding consistently, while supporting routine Publications administration, ordering stationery and supplies, and undertaking related activities within your capabilities.

About You:
You will bring strong written English, excellent attention to detail and a practical approach to explaining technical information. Experience in technical writing, technical publications or procedure writing is essential, alongside the confidence to question, clarify and verify information with technical specialists.

You should be comfortable managing several tasks, following work through to completion and taking responsibility for accuracy. Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel, together with a good understanding of page layout and image manipulation using desktop-publishing software, is required.

Experience in a regulated or quality-controlled industry, particularly medical devices, would be valuable. title: Event Project Coordinator
description:
Hybrid working: 4 days in office

Luxury and mass-market automotive brand experiences, media launches and test drive programmes across multiple continents, and day-to-day ownership of live project elements from the start. An Event Project Coordinator role inside a specialist agency with retained blue-chip clients and a portfolio that opens doors.
- Clear progression: Event Project Coordinator to PM to Senior PM
- BUPA healthcare from probation
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, office closed over Christmas and New Year
- Global luxury and mass-market automotive projects for your portfolio
- Electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme

The Company

This is a specialist automotive experiential agency, part of a 40-year-old global organisation, working exclusively across media launches, test drive programmes, brand experiences, conferencing and retailer training. The team has tripled in size since COVID and is continuing to grow. Retained blue-chip clients and a reputation for long-term relationships mean the work is consistent and the portfolio is genuinely impressive.

The Role

As Event Project Coordinator, you will support client leads and project managers across a broad mix of projects, taking day-to-day ownership of smaller events and defined elements of larger builds, with budgets ranging from £10,000 to £1 million across the UK and internationally.
- Coordinate logistics and planning across multiple concurrent projects
- Support project managers on media launches, experiential and test drive programmes
- Manage supplier communications and track project timelines
- Assist with budget monitoring and purchase order administration
- Liaise with clients and internal teams to keep projects on track
- Contribute to onsite delivery across UK and international events

The Candidate

You will already have event coordination or project support experience behind you, and the organisational habits and communication skills that the Event Project Coordinator role demands. You are comfortable managing multiple priorities under pressure, precise with detail and genuinely adaptable when plans shift.

Experience in automotive, luxury brand events or experiential programmes is beneficial but not essential. Exposure to multi-location logistics, supplier management or budget tracking will strengthen your application. Candidates from adjacent event backgrounds are very welcome to apply as an Event Project Coordinator.

Structured career development, BUPA healthcare, a generous holiday allowance and high-profile automotive work across global markets are all on the table here. Interviews are being confirmed now, so get your application across today.

description: PREVIOUS APPLICANTS NEED NOT APPLY Advert - Band 3 Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator - Urology We have some exciting opportunities available to join the Urology team as a Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator. We have a variety of posts based at either the Churchill Hospital (Headington) or the Horton Hospital (Banbury). As a Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator, you will work closely with our clinical teams to support the delivery of excellent care to our patients. Your day-to-day role will involve talking with patients and the clinical teams, carrying out a variety of administrative tasks such as booking clinic appointments, scheduling patients into an operating theatre list, and making sure our consultant and nursing teams' clinic letters are processed and sent out to our patients. These roles are ideal for anyone looking to move into the NHS, with good opportunities for career progression both within and outside the department. We welcome applications from recent school leavers or graduates, or those looking for a change, as full training will be given once you start in your role. Informal discussions or visits to the department are welcomed, please do contact either Lisha Collier or Sandra Hardy (Urology Pathway Managers) for further information. Lisha.Collier@ouh.nhs.uk Sandra.Hardy@ouh.nhs.uk 1. Book new and follow-up outpatient and diagnostic appointments, ensuring that capacity is proactively and efficiently used. This includes booking patients into the correct clinic to ensure that they are seen by the most appropriate clinician. 2. Reschedule outpatient appointments as a result of patients calling the service, in line with local targets and agreed local processes in respect to patient cancellations. 3. Actively review patient DNAs, liaising with the appropriate clinical staff and reschedule patient appointments in line with agreed local processes. 4. Taking telephone calls from patients and actioning their queries or directing them to the appropriate person. 5. Contributing to the management of the daily emails accounts within the department, ensuring that queries are dealt with effectively and efficiently. 6. Completing clinical letters for patients and GPs 7. Adding additional clinic capacity on EPR as directed by management. 8. Liaise with the appropriate teams (e.g. learning disabilities team, translator services etc) to ensure that patients requiring additional support services are not indirectly discriminated. The post holder will be expected to provide day to day administrative support for Urology clinicians within the Urology department. The individual will need to be flexible to meet the competing and evolving demands of the service. There will be an element of cross cover required within the team and an extension of the role to provide administrative support to other services covered by the Urology Team Patient administration underpins the patient journey and supports clinical teams in delivering high quality patient care and can make a real difference to the patient experience. Effective and efficient patient administration supports management through ensuring a high standard of data quality and by making the best use of capacity and resources. The post holder has responsibility for the provision of a professional, comprehensive, and efficient administrative support service for the Urology clinical team
